best_for: Linux users, and Windows users who like KDE tools, who want a free multi-file text editor with LSP code completion and a built-in terminal, without the weight of a full IDE.

points.title: Many files, one window
points.text: Kate opens many files in tabs or split views, with a project sidebar for folders. Multi-cursor editing, a vi mode and rectangular selection are built in.

points.title: Code smarts through LSP
points.text: Autocompletion for many languages comes from the Language Server Protocol, and Kate highlights over 400 languages.

points.title: Plugins come preinstalled
points.text: Default plugins include an embedded terminal, SQL queries, GDB debugging, one-click builds and a preview for Markdown, HTML and SVG.

points.title: Mac builds are nightlies
points.text: KDE's download page offers only nightly builds for macOS, for Intel and Apple Silicon, and warns they may be unstable. The macOS build listed here needs macOS 13 and is the current release only.

points.title: Windows: Store or nightly
points.text: KDE points Windows users to the Microsoft Store and labels its own installer as a nightly for testing. The installer here can install per-user or for all users, and the Windows listing keeps 28 versions.

points.title: At home on Linux
points.text: Most distributions package Kate. The Flathub build is published by KDE and marked verified, for x64 and Arm64, at about 10 MB to download.
